claims.text:
ranking-top-heavy

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:ranking-top-heavy` → `ai-ranking-top-heavy` → `src/demos/ai/ai-ranking-top-heavy`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/170`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30f.md#3-ranking-top-heavy`. **Packet:** C1. **Level / prerequisites:** stretch; `ai:auc-ranking`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** auc-ranking treats pairwise ordering; this metric prices the same relevance swap differently by rank.

**Computed primary model:** Four binary relevances[1,0,1,0]. DCG=sum relevance_i/log2(rank_i+1), rank1..4, no normalization. Original1.5. Swap first two→[0,1,1,0], DCG1/log2(3)+.5≈1.1309298, loss.3690702. Swap last two→[1,0,0,1], DCG1+1/log2(5)≈1.4306766, loss.0693234. Each swaps the same1/0 relevance pair, isolating position weights.

**Countercase / boundary:** Unweighted relevance sum remains2 in every ordering; a metric with no rank discount would not show this difference. These declared weights are not evidence of universal human utility or that every ranking metric is equally top-heavy.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict which equal-relevance swap loses more DCG; recall a lower-rank swap can preserve the item count and still lower a discounted score.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Swap top/Swap bottom computes per-rank contributions and totals on the same four-row list, retaining both loss values. Display discount rule and raw relevance before commitment, hide computed score until earned.

**Source obligation:** Declared finite construction and reproduced arithmetic support only this toy.
